subject: MeadowHealth — request for customer scenarios, edge cases, and redaction guidance
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@meadowhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MeadowHealth — request for customer scenarios, edge cases, and redaction guidance

Hi Elena — great demo today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and asks so we can scope the eval properly: 

- Primary goal: MeadowHealth wants a model for clinical triage suggestions (non-diagnostic), patient-message drafting, and internal note summarization.
- Key constraints: must avoid returning any direct PHI, need predictable 95th%-tile latency < 450ms for 1-2 user concurrent flows, and budget guidance for monthly active users ~10k.

Could you do the following items by EOD next Tuesday (Dec 1)?
1) Upload a set of 30–50 representative customer prompts / example conversations that capture the happy path and the 8–10 most common edge cases (confusing symptoms, ambiguous insurance details, multi-lingual snippets). Use the attached prompt_samples_template.csv to keep columns consistent (prompt_text, expected_output, sensitivity_flag).
2) Flag sensitive fields you consider PHI or PII and include guidance on what to redact versus pseudonymize. If you have a procurement or security contact, please include them (we'll need to kick off a short SOC2 evidence ask later).
3) Share any benchmark or SLAs you already track for response times or throughput.

We recommend uploading files to this Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMeadowPromptUpld (we can set perms). If it's easier, you can reply with a small sample inline and attach a CSV.

Ben/Marissa — looping you in for model-fit advice and an initial eval plan after Elena sends the samples. My suggested timeline: sample intake by 12/1, draft eval + model recommendation by 12/5, short internal sync on 12/6.

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Thanks Elena — sample received and looks useful. Two quick clarifications that will help our redaction advice: 

1) For any direct identifiers (MRN, SSN, full DOB) please remove them or replace with a token (e.g., [MRN_REDACTED]). For dates, if relative timing matters, please use offsets ("3 days ago") rather than absolute DOBs.
2) For multi-lingual examples, include the language tag in a separate column (template supports this).

I'll attach our short redaction checklist in the Drive folder and share a recommended pseudonymization pattern. If procurement wants a sanitized checklist to sign off before we accept raw exports, we can include that as part of the intake.

Connor

Ben/Marissa — forwarding the thread + sample Elena sent. Ask below: can you review the attached partial sample and respond with: 

- Short model recommendation (2-3 model variants) with reasoning for quality vs cost tradeoffs for triage / note summary / message drafting.
- Any guardrails we should add to the eval (prompt templates, expected outputs, automatic rejection heuristics).
- A lightweight benchmark plan: 95th%-tile latency targets, token-cost estimate for 10k MAU, and a rough eval script we can run once they upload full CSV.

Key concerns to address in your reply: 
- Quality regression: MeadowHealth is highly sensitive to hallucinations in clinical note summaries; propose 2–3 eval prompts that specifically test omission/commission errors and instruction-following.
- Redaction: include recommended pseudonymization pattern (we should mention tokenization effects on privacy-sensitive spans).

Timeline: Elena expects sample intake by 12/1; can we have a recommended model + benchmark plan ready by EOD 12/5? If you need more samples to size the eval, flag it in your reply and I'll ask for them.

I'll attach the eval_plan_template.md in the Drive folder for your edits: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMeadowPromptUpld

Thanks — Connor
